en: Can you give me a little discount on this?
context: Asking a shopkeeper for a lower price.
explain: Can you ...? is a polite way to ask. 'A little' makes the request softer.

alt.en: Could you reduce the price a bit?

en: This is too expensive, I will not pay that much.
tamil: இது ரொம்ப விலை அதிகம், அவ்வளவு கொடுக்க மாட்டேன்.
context: Refusing a high price while bargaining.
explain: 'Too' means more than is good. 'Will not' shows a firm decision.

en: What is your last price for two shirts?
tamil: ரெண்டு சட்டைக்கு உங்க கடைசி விலை என்ன?
context: Final bargaining question in a market.
explain: 'Last price' is common Indian English for the lowest price. It is a natural thing to say while bargaining.

en: If you give it for four hundred, I will take both.
context: Making an offer to the seller.
explain: This is an if-sentence. After 'if' we use the present tense, and the result uses 'will'.

alt.en: I will take both if you make it four hundred.

en: Please show me the same shirt in medium size.
context: Asking a salesperson for another size.
explain: 'Please' plus a base verb makes a polite request. 'In medium size' tells the size you want.

en: Do you have this in a bigger size?
context: Looking for a larger size in a clothes shop.
explain: 'Do you have...?' is the usual way to ask if a shop has something. 'Bigger' compares two sizes.

en: The trial room is on the second floor.
context: Telling someone where to try clothes.
explain: 'Trial room' is what Indians usually call the changing room. We use 'on' with floors.

en: This kurta is a little tight around the shoulders.
tamil: இந்த குர்தா தோள்ல கொஞ்சம் இறுக்கமா இருக்கு.
context: Telling the seller that the fit is not right.
explain: 'A little' makes the complaint gentle. 'Tight' is the opposite of loose.

en: I have been looking for a good pair of sandals all day.
tamil: நாள் முழுக்க நல்ல செருப்பு ஒரு ஜோடி தேடிக்கிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Complaining after a long day of shopping.
explain: 'Have been looking' shows an action that started earlier and is still going on. 'A pair of' is used for sandals and shoes.

en: We went to the mall yesterday, but nothing was on sale.
tamil: நேத்து மால் போனோம், ஆனா எதுவும் தள்ளுபடியில இல்ல.
context: Telling a friend about a shopping trip.
explain: 'Went' and 'was' are past tense. 'On sale' means sold at a lower price.

en: Is there a food court in this mall?
context: Asking about eating places inside a mall.
explain: 'Is there...?' asks if something exists in a place. 'In this mall' tells the place.

en: Let us meet near the parking lot at six.
context: Fixing a meeting point at the mall.
explain: 'Let us' is used to suggest a plan together. 'Near' means close to a place.

en: The vegetable seller always gives me extra coriander.
tamil: காய்கறிக்காரர் எப்பவும் எனக்கு கூடுதலா கொத்தமல்லி தருவார்.
context: Talking about a friendly market seller.
explain: 'Always' with a present verb shows a habit. 'Extra' means more than normal.

en: Tomatoes are costing sixty rupees a kilo these days.
tamil: இப்போ தக்காளி கிலோ அறுபது ரூபாய் ஆகுது.
context: Complaining about rising vegetable prices.
explain: 'These days' goes with the present continuous for a changing situation. 'A kilo' means for each kilo.

en: Please weigh it again, I think it is less.
tamil: தயவுசெஞ்சு மறுபடி எடை போடுங்க, குறைவா இருக்குன்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Doubting the weight of what you bought.
explain: 'Again' means one more time. 'I think' makes the doubt polite.

en: I do not need a bag, I brought my own.
tamil: எனக்கு பை வேண்டாம், நானே கொண்டு வந்திருக்கேன்.
context: Refusing a plastic bag at the counter.
explain: 'Do not need' refuses politely. 'Brought' is the past of 'bring'.

en: Will you please keep the change for the next time?
context: Asking a shopkeeper to adjust a small balance later.
explain: 'Will you please' is a very polite request. Here 'change' means the money returned to you.

en: I will pay by UPI, is that fine?
context: Asking whether digital payment is accepted.
explain: 'By UPI' tells the method of payment. We say 'pay by' card, cash or UPI.

en: The payment failed, but my money got deducted.
context: Complaining about a failed online payment.
explain: 'Got deducted' is a common spoken way to say money was taken from your account.

en: Don't share your OTP with anyone.
context: Warning a friend about safe online payment.
explain: 'Don't' plus a base verb gives a warning or an order. 'Anyone' means any person at all.

en: Can I get a bill for this, please?
context: Asking for a bill at the counter.
explain: 'Can I get...?' is a simple polite request. A bill is the written proof of your purchase.
